rule.title: Visa Fraud Monitoring Program
rule.note: This reason code generally cannot be represented. Recommend accepting liability unless the merchant can prove the transaction was miscoded by the issuer.

summary.allegation: The issuer has charged back a £78.50 transaction of 30 April 2025 at Brightline Beauty under the Visa Fraud Monitoring Program, asserting the transaction was identified as fraudulent through Visa's fraud monitoring of the merchant.
summary.to_defend: Visa 10.5 can only be defended by showing the transaction was miscoded by the issuer under the Fraud Monitoring Program — i.e. it was not a fraudulent transaction and should not have been reported as such.

requirements.title: Proof the issuer miscoded the chargeback
requirements.text: Evidence that the transaction was miscoded by the issuer under the Visa Fraud Monitoring Program.
requirements.finding: The merchant's records show a fully authenticated, address-matched and delivered transaction: Visa Secure authentication with ECI 05 for txn_1178ST, AVS 'Y' and CVV 'M', and Evri delivery on 2 May 2025 to 22 Cavendish Court, SW4 7QR — the same postcode as the billing address — signed for by 'WHITFORD', on a returning account with three prior undisputed orders. That is strong evidence the transaction was not fraudulent, but there is no issuer or Visa record directly confirming the transaction was miscoded under the Fraud Monitoring Program.
requirements.gap: No documentation from the issuer or Visa confirming the fraud coding was applied in error; the miscoding argument is inferential from the authentication and delivery evidence.

justification: Full Visa Secure authentication (ECI 05) with AVS/CVV match and signed delivery to the billing postcode supports the argument that the transaction was wrongly coded as fraud.
rationale: The issuer has charged back £78.50 (txn_1178ST, 30 April 2025) under the Visa Fraud Monitoring Program. The transaction was successfully authenticated through Visa Secure with ECI 05 and a valid CAVV at 22:14:51 UTC on 30 April 2025, and carried AVS result 'Y' and CVV result 'M'. Order BB-77231 for £78.50 was delivered by Evri (tracking H7821VV) on 2 May 2025 at 14:08 to 22 Cavendish Court, London SW4 7QR — matching the billing postcode on file — and was signed for by 'WHITFORD', on a returning customer account with three prior undisputed orders since January 2025. These facts are inconsistent with a fraudulent transaction and indicate the item was miscoded as fraud under the Fraud Monitoring Program. We represent on that basis, while noting that no issuer-side confirmation of the coding error is available to us.
